concerns.message: The design gives the bolt "an id used only in events", so a bolt hit or block produces a DuelEvent whose moveId is not in `moveset.moves`. `restoreDuel` checks every event's moveId with `oneOf(...moveset.moves.map(id))` (packages/simulation/src/duel/snapshot.ts:129,156), so it refuses any snapshot taken on the frame a bolt makes contact. No acceptance item catches this. Item 6 restores in the middle of a projectile's flight, usually on a frame with no events. The property tests in item 5 compare replay hashes and never restore. The existing test that accepts the step's snapshots only covers the Duelist trace. Fix before starting: the event check must accept each kit's projectile id (ideally only for the attacker's kit). Add an acceptance line: every state of every kit property run round-trips through snapshotDuel → JSON → restoreDuel to the same hash.
concerns.consequence: In fruit-kits-online the server sends a full snapshot every 6 frames. When one lands on a bolt-contact frame, `restoreDuel` throws inside the client's rollback session (netcode/rollback.ts:297/304), so an Ember duel breaks online. This feature's checks would all pass, so nobody would see it until then.

concerns.message: By the design's only non-striking rule (only moves with `projectile` or `zone` data don't strike), the feint strikes with its required hitbox on its active frames, and its damage and hitstun must be positive. So the 'feint' is really an advancing attack that strikes pass through during startup: a Duelist thrust with a reversal attached. Also, `advance` runs through startup and active frames while `strikeInvulnerable` ≤ startup, so 'strike invulnerability ends with the dash' only holds if the feint has 1 active frame. Either make the feint explicitly non-striking (for example `cancel` data implies no strike) or state that it strikes, with damage below the Duelist's thrust.
concerns.consequence: The worker picks one silently. If it strikes, Smoke gets an invulnerable-startup approach attack that cancels into normals, which undercuts 'low direct damage'. It also puts the feint into the start-gap reach check and into the renderer's hitbox drawing. The matchup tests would then prove a different kit from §9's.

concerns.message: No acceptance item checks symmetry for the new entities. The step promises that 'neither fighter is processed first', but bolt meets bolt, melee priority, bolt beats grab and zone marking are all new pairwise resolution code where a slot-0-first loop is easy to write. The existing `expectMirrored` harness in determinism.test.ts already catches this for the Duelist.
concerns.consequence: A slot-order bias (for example player one's bolt surviving a meeting, or winning a same-frame trade) passes every listed test. It only shows up online, as desyncs in who wins trades, depending on which seat a player got.

concerns.message: The golden traces record only position, velocity, health, stamina, action and action frame. They miss moveId, timer, facing, combo, buffer, crouching, moveHit, events, phase and result. The Duelist fighter's new state is just the default kit field, so the fixture could hold the whole canonical fighter state without `kit`, plus events, phase and result, for about the same cost.
concerns.consequence: A regression in buffer consumption, combo counting, event ordering or moveHit can reproduce the six traced fields for a stretch, or drift only near the end of a round, and still pass the 'mirror unchanged' proof that decisions.md relies on for the parallel merge.

concerns.message: The block rule is worded 'hold away from the bolt's direction of travel', which read literally means holding toward the bolt's source. The intended rule, which generalises the existing `input.h === awayFrom(def, att)`, is to guard when `h` equals the bolt's travel direction.
concerns.consequence: If the worker takes it literally, an ordinary bolt is blocked by holding forward. Tests written by the same worker would pass, and the renderer and players would get an inverted guard.

concerns.message: Bolt contacts (bolt against bolt, and bolt against a hurtbox) are presumably checked by overlap at discrete frame positions. Two bolts closing at 2×speed pass through each other without ever overlapping when 2×speed ≥ the sum of their widths. The same happens against a thin airborne hurtbox.
concerns.consequence: The contact rule 'bolts cancel each other' fails at some spacings, and only the random property runs would hit that, nondeterministically across tuning. Add a schema check (2×speed < bolt width) or use a swept test.

concerns.message: The Duelist's specials would be listed twice (`commands.special1/2` and `kits.duelist`), and `restoreDuel` accepts any move id for any fighter. The schema should require that the two lists agree, and `restoreDuel` should refuse a fighter whose moveId belongs to another kit's specials.
concerns.consequence: Otherwise the data can drift: the step reads `kits`, while anything reading `commands` sees other moves. A tampered or corrupt snapshot could also put a Duelist mid-flare, and it would be accepted and hashed.

concerns.message: `apps/web/src/arenaScene.ts:56-79` draws `move.hitbox` and colours the fighter red for any attack move on its active frames. The bolt cast and screen cast (and the feint, if it doesn't strike) keep a required but inert hitbox, so the development view will show fake melee hitboxes. Export the non-striking rule as a helper from the duel module and record it in docs/fruit-kits.md for fruit-kits-online.
concerns.consequence: fruit-kits-online's renderer would show attacks that can't connect. That is exactly the readability §8 and §9 guard against, and the rule would be duplicated outside the simulation.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Store the new entities as fixed per-fighter slots (`bolt: Bolt | null`, `zone: Zone | null` in FighterState, or a fixed-length pair) instead of top-level lists that need bounds. 'At most one per fighter' then holds by construction. `restoreDuel`'s existing `exactly<FighterState>` check validates them with no separate count logic. The symmetry harness's fighter swap carries them along, and the invariant in the property test can't break. Pair that with an explicit non-striking marker for the feint and the casts, as one exported `strikesWithHitbox(move)` helper used by the step, the start-gap check and later the renderer. That removes the implicit 'projectile or zone means no strike' rule.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before choosing Ember's data, spend about 30 minutes checking with the current body data that the bolt tests can all pass together. With jumpVelocity 160, gravity 8 and jumpSpeedX 40, a jumper's feet are above the crouching hurtbox top (56 px, which a mid bolt must reach) only on about jump frames 7 to 32, and the jump moves 100 px. Script traceDuel with a Duelist forward-jumping from mid range, then search bolt spawn offset, box height and speed, and the cast's active + recovery. Every one of these must hold: (a) the bolt passes under the jumper within that window; (b) the landing leaves the heavy's 80 px reach, and Ember's remaining cast is longer than landing + the heavy's 18-frame startup (about 59 frames from the jump); (c) a second bolt after a hit arrives after the hitstun ends, so it can be blocked; (d) the flare's box catches jump heights the anti-air misses (feet above 144 px, or beyond 66 px). If no combination fits within §8's floors, the jump-over test and 'punishes jumps' conflict, and the bolt's guard height or the acceptance wording has to change before any step code is written.
